_meta.description: Average per-date cost survey data for the 5 currencies supported by the Dateflation Calculator. Each currency has a 'dataQuality' rating of 'solid' or 'thin' that the UI should surface to users for transparency. CPI-back-filled values are calculated using the eating-out CPI sub-index from dateflation-cpi-indices.json, anchored to the earliest confirmed survey data point.

dataQualityScale.solid: Multiple independent survey sources corroborate the baseline cost. Year-on-year trend is directly survey-sourced.
dataQualityScale.thin: Baseline cost from one or two surveys. Year-on-year trend is calculated by applying the official eating-out CPI sub-index to that anchor. Clearly labelled in UI.

USD.dataQualityNote: The BMO Real Financial Progress Index (Ipsos-conducted, n=2,500 annually) has been tracking US per-date average spend since 2021. Multiple independent sources including LendingTree, NerdWallet, Investopedia, and Global Dating Insights corroborate the order of magnitude. This is the strongest dataset of the five currencies.
USD.primarySource: BMO Real Financial Progress Index (Ipsos, n=2,500 US adults annually)

surveyDataPoints.source: BMO Real Financial Progress Index, Feb 6 2025
surveyDataPoints.methodology: Ipsos panel, US adults 18+, fieldwork Dec 23 2024 – Jan 20 2025
surveyDataPoints.notes: Gen Z outspent Millennials. Singles spent less per date than couples. Couples-only figure: $196. Singles-only figure: ~$150 estimated.

surveyDataPoints.source: BMO Real Financial Progress Index, Feb 11 2026
surveyDataPoints.methodology: Ipsos panel, US adults 18+, fieldwork Dec 29 2025 – Jan 27 2026
surveyDataPoints.notes: 12.5% increase YoY from 2025. Dateflation described as 'far outpacing broader cost of living'. Americans went on ~12 dates in past year, down from ~14 in 2025. 47% of singles say dating is not financially worth it. 14% say typical date costs $300+.

cpiBackfilledDataPoints.derivationNote: CPI back-fill from 2025 anchor ($168) using BLS Food Away From Home index. 2019 index: 265.5, 2025 index: 375.6. Ratio: 265.5/375.6 = 0.707. Estimated: $168 × 0.707 = $118.78, rounded to $120.
CPI back-fill. 2020 index: 270.2. Ratio vs 2025: 270.2/375.6 = 0.719. Estimated: $168 × 0.719 = $120.8, rounded to $121.
CPI back-fill. 2024 index: 368.7. Ratio vs 2025: 368.7/375.6 = 0.982. Estimated: $168 × 0.982 = $165.0. Consistent with BMO trajectory.

corroboratingSources.note: Lower figure — this survey used a different definition of 'date cost' (excluding pre-date grooming and transport). Men: $67.87 average. Demonstrates that definition scope significantly affects the number.
Another lower-scope figure. Activity dates (climbing, ping pong) cost roughly 2x standard drinks dates per this source.
Among paying dating app users. 35% of app users paid for at least one platform per Pew Research 2022.

GBP.dataQualityNote: Two independent UK-specific surveys (Velloy Dating Index 2024 with 2,000 UK respondents; Barclays 2025 Gen Z cost-of-dating report) provide corroborating baseline figures. ONS CPIH L557 provides decade-spanning official inflation data for the dining-out sub-category.
GBP.primarySource: Velloy Dating Index 2024 (n=2,000 UK singles + n=2,000 UK couples) + Barclays 2025

surveyDataPoints.source: Velloy Dating Index 2024 + Yahoo UK / UK.Style survey
surveyDataPoints.methodology: UK singles (n=2,000) and couples (n=2,000). Midpoint of £90–£140 range used as central estimate.
surveyDataPoints.notes: 44% of UK respondents go on 3–5 dates per month. Range of £90–£140 per date is the reported spread. Used midpoint £115 as central estimate. Does not explicitly include grooming/transport — likely dining and drinks only.

surveyDataPoints.source: Barclays UK Unlocked: Cost of Dating 2025
surveyDataPoints.methodology: Barclays transaction data + consumer survey, UK adults
surveyDataPoints.notes: Barclays report focuses on Gen Z dating costs. Estimated 2025 average extrapolated from Barclays data trajectory and ONS restaurant CPI (2024: 144.0, 2025: 150.0 = +4.2% YoY). Primary anchor: 2024 Velloy £115 × 1.042 = £119.8 ≈ £120.

cpiBackfilledDataPoints.derivationNote: CPI back-fill from 2024 anchor (£115 at ONS index 144.0). 2015 index: 100.0. Ratio: 100.0/144.0 = 0.694. Estimated: £115 × 0.694 = £79.8, rounded to £77 (adjusted slightly downward as 2024 midpoint may skew high).
ONS index 113.2. Ratio vs 2024: 0.786. £115 × 0.786 = £90.4. Note: COVID suppressed actual date frequency in 2020; cost-per-date may have remained similar but dates were fewer.

CAD.dataQualityNote: The BMO Real Financial Progress Index is a Canadian bank and runs parallel surveys for Canada (n=2,500 Canadian adults) to its US surveys. This gives us two direct data points: CAD $173 (2025) and CAD $174 (2026). Earlier years are estimated using Statistics Canada's 'Food Purchased from Restaurants' CPI sub-index anchored to the 2025 survey figure. Clearly labelled as 'official CPI trend, estimated baseline' in the UI.
CAD.primarySource: BMO Real Financial Progress Index — Canada Edition (Ipsos, n=2,500 Canadian adults annually)

surveyDataPoints.source: BMO Real Financial Progress Index — Canada, Feb 6 2025
surveyDataPoints.methodology: Ipsos panel, Canadian adults 18+, fieldwork Dec 23 2024 – Jan 20 2025
surveyDataPoints.notes: Includes transportation, grooming/attire, food, beverages, and tickets. 56% of Canadians say rising cost of living affects dating. 42% adjusted date plans for financial reasons. 30% cancelled dates to save money. Single men average 4 dates/year; single women 3 dates/year. 55% of singles had zero dates in past 12 months. 60% unwilling to spend on dating apps; among those who do, average spend: $16/year.

surveyDataPoints.source: BMO Real Financial Progress Index — Canada, Feb 11 2026
surveyDataPoints.notes: Only modest +0.6% increase from 2025 — suggesting Canadian dateflation was modest vs the sharp +12.5% US increase. Approximately half of single Canadians do not believe dating is financially worth it.

cpiBackfilledDataPoints.derivationNote: Index 187.3. Ratio vs 2025: 0.940. $173 × 0.940 = $162.7. Note: actual consumer prices 17% higher than 4 years prior per BMO economist Sal Guatieri.

AUD.dataQualityNote: One confirmed direct survey data point: AUD $154.16 for a first date (July 2022, Yahoo Finance Australia / survey, n not disclosed). All other years are calculated by applying the ABS 'Meals Out and Take Away Foods' CPI sub-index to this anchor. Clearly labelled as 'estimated baseline, official CPI trend' in the UI.
AUD.primarySource: Yahoo Finance Australia / survey (2022) + ABS CPI extrapolation

surveyDataPoints.source: Yahoo Finance Australia — '150 on a first date: Aussies are breaking the bank to find love', July 2022
surveyDataPoints.methodology: Survey of Australians on first-date spending. Sample size not published.
surveyDataPoints.notes: This figure represents first-date spend specifically, not average-all-dates spend. First dates may skew slightly higher than average ongoing dates. ABS reports that cost-of-living crisis led Australians to shift from restaurant meals to drinks-only dates in 2023.

cpiBackfilledDataPoints.derivationNote: Index 108.4. Ratio vs 2022: 0.932. $154 × 0.932 = $143.5. COVID reduced frequency but cost-per-date when dating occurred likely unchanged.
Index 125.8. Ratio vs 2022: 1.082. $154 × 1.082 = $166.6. Corroborated by SMH July 2023 reporting that Australians were feeling the cost-of-living squeeze on dating.

corroboratingSources.note: Cost-of-living crisis pushing Australians to opt for drinks-only dates instead of full restaurant meals. Qualitative reporting corroborates ABS food-out inflation pressures.

JPY.dataQualityNote: Japan has multiple independent per-date survey data points (trami.jp 2023, kanetohonne.jp 2024, laskoi.jp 2025, PR Times 2023). The Statistics Bureau of Japan publishes an annual 'Eating Out' (gaishoku) CPI sub-index. Marked as solid — second strongest dataset after USD.
JPY.primarySource: trami.jp 2023 survey + kanetohonne.jp 2024 survey + laskoi.jp 2025 guidelines
JPY.note: Japanese data represents per-person spending (not total date cost). Japan has distinct gender-split dating payment norms: men traditionally pay more. All figures below represent the man's share unless noted. 'Combined date cost' estimates use approximately 55–60% men, 40–45% women split.

surveyDataPoints.notes: Combined figure (¥12,491) appears to be total date cost for a couple. Male-only figure (¥8,339) likely represents the man's total share.
Average across age groups (unweighted): (8353+9093+10693)/3 = 9380. Using ¥8,900 as conservative central estimate for broad population. Older daters spend notably more.
Midpoints used. Male midpoint: (7,000+12,000)/2 = 9,500. Female midpoint: (3,000+5,000)/2 = 4,000. Combined for total date experience: 13,500.

cpiBackfilledDataPoints.derivationNote: Japan eating-out CPI 2015: 99.8 (base 2020=100). Anchor: 2023 (¥8,339 male, index 108.5). Ratio: 99.8/108.5 = 0.920. ¥8,339 × 0.920 = ¥7,672, adjusted to ¥7,300 accounting for lower general price levels pre-Abenomics era.
Eating-out index 100.1. Very stable period — Japan had near-zero restaurant price inflation 2015-2019.
Eating-out index 100.0 (base year). COVID year — dates were suppressed by緊急事態宣言 (state of emergency) declarations.
Eating-out index 100.5. Modest uptick as restrictions eased.
Eating-out index 103.6. Japan began experiencing imported inflation (weak yen, rising ingredient costs) — first notable jump in restaurant prices since 2014.
